mean_edge_error — 3D pose_graph op

• Data kinds: pose → measurement

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.mean_edge_error(poses, edges) (to call the implementation directly, import pose_graph; pose_graph.mean_edge_error(poses, edges); from the registry, ops3d.get("mean_edge_error"))

Usage

The RMS of the edge residuals (how consistent the pose graph is). → scalar.

For each edge (i, j, rvec_meas, t_meas[, w_rot, w_trans]), turns the discrepancy measured⁻¹ ∘ predicted between the predicted relative pose T_i⁻¹ ∘ T_j and the measurement (rvec_meas, t_meas) into a 6-dimensional residual of 3 rotation-vector components + 3 translation components (multiplied by sqrt(w_rot) and sqrt(w_trans) respectively; weights default to 1 if omitted), and returns the root of the mean of the 2nd powers over all edges and all components. Same quantity as rmse returned by optimize_pose_graph; use it to compare before and after optimisation.

• poses: [rvec | t] reshapeable to (N,6) (world←body).

• edges: list of the tuples above. Returns 0.0 if empty.

Caution: rotation components (rad) and translation components (coordinate units) are averaged in the same array, so the value has mixed dimensions. In scenes with a large translation scale the translation terms dominate; to align units, weight with w_rot / w_trans. This function does not validate the edge index range (a negative index silently refers to another node via numpy's wrap-around; optimize_pose_graph does validate).
